name: Communication
description: Ability to communicate security findings, risks, and recommendations effectively to diverse audiences. Covers client-facing communication, technical briefings, presentation skills, and the ability to translate complex technical issues for non-technical stakeholders.

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the importance of audience-appropriate communication
evidence: Can distinguish between technical and executive audiences
Understands that findings must be communicated, not just documented

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Participates in client communications under supervision
evidence: Has attended client debriefs and kick-off meetings
Can explain individual findings clearly in verbal discussion
Communication reviewed by senior staff before client delivery

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently leads technical briefings and client communications
evidence: Effectively communicates risk to non-technical stakeholders
Handles client questions and pushback professionally

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles sensitive and high-stakes communications; mentors on presentation skills
evidence: Leads communications for complex, multi-stakeholder engagements
Delivers findings to board-level or regulatory audiences
Coaches junior staff on communication and presentation

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's communication standards; recognized thought leader; trains teams
evidence: Keynotes or invited talks at major industry conferences
Defines communication standards and templates adopted across the lab
Trains teams on technical communication and stakeholder management

assessment_methods.description: Observe a client debrief or technical presentation led by the individual
Scenario: explain a complex vulnerability chain to a non-technical executive audience
